1.explanation:
1. lib/features/replace/BpmnReplace.js – this is the core replacement handler; it builds a new business object when you change from parallel to sequential and applies only a whitelist of properties. The filter for ‘loopCharacteristics’ is generic and doesn’t preserve existing multi-instance sub-properties, so your loop cardinality and other settings get dropped when toggling.

2. lib/features/replace/ReplaceOptions.js – this defines the replace menu entries for parallel vs. sequential multi-instance. Its options set only the top-level instantiate/isSequential flags on the businessObject, but never carry forward the user-configured loopCharacteristics (e.g. loopCardinality), so BpmnReplace never sees them to copy.

3. lib/features/modeling/cmd/UpdateModdlePropertiesHandler.js – this command is used when toggling properties via the properties panel. It writes new values onto the moddle element, but because the replacement path creates a brand-new loopCharacteristics element (or sets only one field), it effectively overwrites or replaces the entire loopCharacteristics, wiping out other nested settings.
1.bug_scenario: The user configures a subprocess (or task) as a parallel multi-instance by setting loop cardinality and then flips the toggle to sequential multi-instance. Immediately after switching, all of the previously configured multi-instance settings (e.g. loop cardinality) vanish, so the element loses its loopCharacteristics.
